critical_code_review_comments: operations.py POST /materials: no unique index or dup-name check — two materials with the same name can be created. Consider unique(name) or a 409 guard.

operations.py GET /materials `low_stock` query filter uses Python-side filtering after the DB fetch — fine at small scale but should be a SQL WHERE on (quantity_on_hand <= reorder_threshold) for large catalogs. Also `low_stock=false` is currently ignored (only truthy triggers filter); passing low_stock=false does NOT return only OK items.

purchasing.py receive(): idempotency check is done BEFORE payload validation, but the row is written AFTER inventory mutations. If two concurrent requests share the same Idempotency-Key, both may pass the initial check_idempotency() (since the row isn't inserted until later) and both could apply inventory deltas before either commits. Consider using a unique constraint + INSERT ... ON CONFLICT and detect duplicates atomically, or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the idempotency row.

purchasing.py receive(): PO status transitions never revert (e.g., cancelled PO check exists but a fully-received PO whose lines are somehow rolled back would remain 'received'). Currently no rollback path, acceptable.
purchasing.py POLineIn.quantity has no gt=0 constraint — a PO line with quantity=0 or negative is currently accepted (line_total=0). Add Field(gt=0).
jobs.py PATCH /api/jobs/{id}: no version/If-Match optimistic concurrency (unlike quotes/estimates). Two concurrent schedule edits will silently last-write-wins.

jobs.py PATCH: valid status list includes 'created','pending','scheduled','in_progress','completed','cancelled' but there is no state-machine enforcement — a completed job can be reverted to 'created'. Acceptable if intentional.
schemas_phase4.MaterialIn: reorder_threshold and quantity_on_hand have no ge=0 constraint — negative starting stock allowed.

operations.py adjust_material: log_action detail includes on_hand + delta, but the InventoryTxn model doesn't record the resulting on_hand value; hard to reconstruct history without replaying all txns.

sales_common.check_idempotency compares entity_type but returns entity_id only — for the receive path, the previous POOut is re-fetched via db.get(PurchaseOrder, po_id); if the passed po_id != prior entity_id (same key used against a different PO), the caller still gets a success response with the CURRENT po. Consider validating prior == po.id and returning 409 otherwise.
purchasing.py: response supplier_name is fetched with an extra db.get per PO in list_pos — N+1 query. Use joinedload(PurchaseOrder.supplier).
operations.py list_suppliers is not filtered by active — inactive suppliers are returned; add optional filter.
